title: Open Jam @ Princeton Public Library
event_description: A welcoming acoustic sing-along in the library's Community Room, with chord charts and lyrics projected for guitar, ukulele, violin, or voice. No experience or sign-up needed, held on select Sunday afternoons throughout the year.
event_time_plain: 3:00 PM - 4:30 PM (dates vary; check library calendar)
hosts: Mike and Judy Seidel (NJ Acoustic Music in the Park)
backline: PA system with a projector screen for chords and lyrics; bring your own acoustic instrument or just your voice
event_venue_information:
Princeton Public Library

A few steps from Palmer Square in downtown Princeton, the Princeton Public Library hosts a periodic Open Acoustic Jam in its Community Room, co-sponsored by NJ Acoustic Music in the Park (NJAMP).

The Open Acoustic Jam

Held on select Sunday afternoons from 3:00 PM to 4:30 PM, the jam is led by longtime NJAMP organizers Mike and Judy Seidel. Chord charts and lyrics are projected on a large screen so participants can sing, strum, or simply listen and clap along. No registration or performance experience is required.

Other Events

The library has also hosted outdoor Listen Local open mic afternoons on Hinds Plaza with the Einstein Alley Musicians Collaborative, giving local musicians a public stage in the center of town.

title: Cafe Improv @ Arts Council of Princeton
event_description: Princeton's long-running monthly open mic for local music, poetry, comedy, and more, staged in the Arts Council's intimate Solley Theater. Beginning and professional performers share one welcoming, informal evening.
backline: House PA and stage sound provided in the Solley Theater
event_venue_information:
Arts Council of Princeton

Housed in the Paul Robeson Center for the Arts, the Arts Council of Princeton runs the monthly Cafe Improv open mic out of its black-box Solley Theater.

Cafe Improv

Now in its fourth decade, Cafe Improv is held monthly on a Saturday evening from 7:00 PM to 10:00 PM. Hosted by John Irving and Tom Florek, the show connects beginning and professional performers across music, poetry, comedy, and more. Admission is $2 general and $1 for Arts Council members; performers can register in advance at cafeimprov.com or sign up at the door.

Other Events

The Arts Council also hosts the monthly Story & Verse poetry and spoken-word open mic in the same theater, alongside a full calendar of gallery exhibitions and classes.
